## Project Overview

We conducted an experimental investigation to quantify the effect of diagonal bracing on the torsional stiffness of a structural assembly. The objective was to understand how introducing diagonal members and triangulating a structure influences its resistance to twisting under an applied torque.

We constructed a custom experimental rig to compare two configurations: an unbraced structure and a diagonally braced (trussed) structure. Torque was applied using rubber bands, while a laser-and-mirror arrangement was used to measure the resulting angular deflection. By comparing the measured responses under equivalent loading conditions, we determined the improvement in torsional rigidity achieved through diagonal bracing.

The results showed that **the diagonally braced structure was 23.25 times more torsionally rigid than the unbraced configuration**. This experiment demonstrated the substantial contribution of diagonal members and structural triangulation to torsional stiffness.

The complete report, including the experimental setup, methodology, measurements, calculations, and analysis, is attached below.



## Experimental Setup

The setup consisted of a base supporting the test structure, attachment points for the rubber-band loading arrangement, and a laser-and-mirror measurement system. The structure was tested in both trussed and untrussed configurations so that their responses could be compared under the experimental arrangement.

![Assembled experimental setup on the workbench.](setup_on_table.JPEG){width=650}

![Rubber-band arrangement used to apply torsion to the test structure.](torsion_by_rubberbands.JPEG){width=650}

## Measurements

The laser-and-mirror arrangement was used to observe the change in the reflected laser position as the structure twisted. Separate readings were recorded for the trussed and untrussed configurations.

![Recorded optical reading for the trussed configuration.](final_reading_truss_1.JPEG){width=650}

![Recorded optical reading for the untrussed configuration.](final_reading_untruss_1.JPEG){width=650}
